not_claimed: No model-quality claim. Every gate in this item is a CPU double over the real production consolidation path; whether GPT-OSS-20B writes an entity-correct digest once the alias turn is gone is the lead's GPU contrast, not this seat's evidence.
No claim that the guard improves fresh recall, corrections, aliases or recap. Those are LT1.1 scorer columns and no CPU fixture here measures them.
No routing claim. The Breakwater routing miss (round-1 top residual, F3) is untouched by this item: F2 changes what is STORED, not what is ranked.

pin_relocations.copy_verified: cmp -s against the r2 source: byte-identical
pin_relocations.why: The pin pointed INSIDE a LIVE campaign run root. r3 resumes into run roots, and a contract pin that requires a file to exist under one makes the frozen r2 receipts load-bearing for a test -- which is how a partial restore of that directory got made in the first place. The manifest is now archived under artifacts/grm_f2/ as a byte-identical copy, so the contract depends on F2's own artifact rather than on the state of someone else's campaign directory.

registered_predictions.abort_risk_named_before_the_run: The attribution QC can abort a fold that coverage would have accepted. Each abort marks its sources no_fold, so a run with many aborts compresses less. Registered expectation: aborts are RARE -- zero on all 13 FIX-5 GPU-contrast folds (tests/test_grm_f2_alias_guard.py::test_control_fix5_gpu_contrast_digests_still_pass). If the r3 arm shows a high abort count, that is a result, not a bug to be tuned away after the fact.
registered_predictions.primary: No digest in the LT1.1 r3 arm-A store is attributed to 'the Beacon' or to any other alias of an entity that does not own the fact. Checkable mechanically: grep the store manifest for digest nodes, run core.grm_fold_alias_guard.attribution_violations over each digest against its recorded sources; expect zero violations across the run.
registered_predictions.residency: The excluded alias turns are NOT retired by the window fold, so the active turn-node population is higher than r2 arm A by the number of exclusions. On the r2 arm-A conversation that is 10 alias turns (the CPU replay itemization in artifacts/grm_d1/alias_cpu_aplus.json lists 10 alias pairs), so expect up to 10 additional un-retired turn nodes and correspondingly more fold windows.
registered_predictions.secondary: Breakwater and Commtower facts stay entity-correct in every digest that carries them; grepping the ON store for 'Breakwater' finds MORE than the r2 arm-A count of 1 node.

resolved_once: in GraftRepository.__init__, so a mid-session environment change cannot alter a repository's fold semantics halfway through a conversation
title: Chronicle fold alias guard
unknown_token_behavior: fails CLOSED to OFF (A1 / L2 / A-DEC precedent)

what_the_lead_pins.arm: LT1.1 r3 arm A only, alias flag GRM_ALIAS_FOLD_MERGE OFF (the r2 arm-A baseline), same frozen conversation, same worker
what_the_lead_pins.env_off_baseline: GRM_FOLD_ALIAS_GUARD unset (do NOT set it to 0 for the baseline arm: absent is the pre-F2 world and is what the byte-identity gate compares against)
what_the_lead_pins.interaction_with_F1: independent env names; F2 changes the fold WINDOW and adds a post-generation QC, F1 (GRM_FOLD_RETAIN_SOURCES) changes what a fold does to its sources afterwards. If both are ON in the same arm, a per-flag attribution cannot be made from that arm alone -- run the flags separately, or accept the joint reading and say so.

when_the_guard_stops_applying: It is a LEXICAL entity proxy (capitalized word, possessive-tolerant), not an entity recognizer. A lower-case entity is invisible to it and the fold behaves exactly as with the flag OFF.
It judges ATTRIBUTION, not truth or completeness. A value the digest never carries raises nothing here -- that stays MIN_FOLD_KEEP's question.
It cannot adjudicate a fact whose source clause names no entity; such a fact is skipped, never guessed.
The alias allowance is scoped to ONE entity: an alias registered for Lantern is accepted in place of Lantern and of nothing else.
